summary.headline: HOEC Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose to INR117.5 crore from negative INR194 crore, but PBT before exceptionals fell to INR12.5 crore on B-80 output loss and HPCL crude resale.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue from operations was INR117.5 crore versus a negative INR194 crore in Q4, which reflected reversal of the HPCL crude sale (INR259 crore). Kharsang output rose from about 12,300 to 17,400 BOE and crude realisation rose to about $95.5/bbl from $70.8/bbl. Standalone PBT before exceptionals fell to INR12.5 crore from INR30.4 crore, due to inventory-related cost offsets. B-80 output was hit by higher water cut, and the HPCL-stored crude is being resold to third parties at a slower pace than expected, with a further mark-to-market loss expected. Management is relying on debt to fund the B-80 workover and three-well programme.

segments.name: Kharsang (Arunachal, crude and gas)
segments.commentary: Output rose from about 12,300 to 17,400 BOE; nine-well programme doubled production year on year and workovers on 23 idle wells are underway (5-6 done). Gas is virgin and unsold for lack of pipeline.

segments.name: B-80 (offshore Mumbai)
segments.commentary: Production reduced by higher water cut from one producing well; compressor configuration changed and in test mode. Crude stored at HPCL Chembur is being sold via tankers; about 15% sold so far. Gas realisation around $15-16/MMBTU on exchange, average $16.5/MMBTU.

segments.name: Dirok (Assam, onshore)
segments.commentary: Operated with ~27% stake; currently producing only 50-70% of well capability due to evacuation limits. DNPL line capacity degraded to ~1-1.5 MMSCMD versus 2.5 MMSCMD design; average gas realisation about $12.5/MMBTU.

segments.name: PY-1 (East Coast, gas)
segments.commentary: Three wells suffered serious production loss; rig-less intervention contracted and funded from own books. Two new wells deferred and contingent on take-or-pay gas agreement with GAIL or IOCL. Realisation about $10-12/MMBTU.

segments.name: Cambay, Gujarat (Asjol, Balol, Palej)
segments.commentary: Palej debottlenecking delivered 5-6% production increase last quarter; management guides 20-30% increase over time. Sucker rod pumps ordered and a new exploration block pending final approval.

segments.name: B-15 (new block)
segments.commentary: Recoverable reserves 16 MMBOE; FDP under preparation with three to four concepts, including tie-back to ONGC platform. Drilling planned in FY28.

guidance_outlook: Dirok: DNPL capacity restoration via hot-tap expected by December 2026, targeted at 2.5 MMSCMD from 1-1.5 MMSCMD; locked-in volumes 0.5-0.7 MMSCMD gross.
B-80: two workovers in Oct-Nov 2026; three new wells (1,000-1,500 bbl/well per simulation, range 700-1,400 or 8,900-13,000 bbl total cited) by June 2027; workovers 500-800 bbl/well.
B-80 crude inventory at HPCL Chembur expected to clear by end-October/early November 2026; sales from FSO in October in 120,000-150,000 bbl tranches.
Management expects further mark-to-market loss of about 7-10% on the remaining HPCL crude; explicitly not guidance.
Kharsang: pipeline route survey tender closing; 24 km pipeline to Bordumsa; 14-18 months to complete; second phase of nine wells pending rig award and tubulars in 1-2 months.
Cash flows expected to fund B-15 by around Nov-Dec 2027; B-80 programme to be funded by debt being raised from market.
capex_capacity: B-80: rig award expected this month; workovers mobilised by October; three wells planned with production from June 2027; jacket and production deck installation required.
PY-1: two new wells deferred until a firm take-or-pay gas agreement; 15-20 MMSCFD potential cited from two wells.
Capex budget increased versus Q4 presentation, which management attributed to a contingency for rig scarcity; facility to be drawn down on need.
Kharsang pipeline: 24 km, 6-8 months for right of way plus 6-8 months for laying; target completion around December 2027 in best case.
Dirok: hot-tap works by Assam Gas Company Ltd and NRL bypass of about 150-200 m of pipeline inside NRL premises.
demand_pricing: Standalone crude/condensate realisation about $95.5/bbl vs $70.8/bbl previous quarter; benefited from favourable Brent.
Gas realisation blended $12/MMBTU vs $9.8 previous quarter; B-80 about $16.5/MMBTU, Dirok about $12.5/MMBTU.
Crude from B-80 resold to third parties; HPCL offtake continues by tanker with gantries added; realisation losses of INR4-6 crore incurred so far.
NRL can act as reseller and sell gas on exchange; management says gas can be sold within about three days once a credible grid path exists.
Oil sales to Digboi Refinery and mainly IOCL from Kharsang.

qa_highlights.question: When will the Northeast grid connectivity for Dirok be complete, and when would Dirok production ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets December 2026 for completion, driven by hot-tap works by Assam Gas Company Ltd and a ~100-200 m NRL bypass; hot-tap lead time quoted at 16-20 weeks, with NRL shutdown no longer needed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of B-80 crude stored at HPCL and when will it clear?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales to third parties via tankers are slower than expected; management hopes the entire HPCL Chembur inventory clears by end-October/early November 2026. About 15% sold so far with INR4-6 crore realisation losses.

qa_highlights.question: How much mark-to-market loss remains on the HPCL crude, and what is standalone EBITDA ex-adjustments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pegged the further loss at 7-10%, explicitly not guidance. The CFO declined to quantify EBITDA excluding inventory and profit petroleum adjustments and promised to revert.

qa_highlights.question: What is the B-80 rig campaign timeline and is the workover plan credible given past failures?
qa_highlights.answer: Two workovers (10-20 days each) after rig mobilisation by October; three wells (30-40 days each) with jacket and production deck, production by June 2027. Management cited rig intervention as higher-confidence than past chemical treatments; 2P reserves of 26 MMboe with 1.5-2 MMboe produced.

qa_highlights.question: Why did capex budget rise versus Q4, and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Increase is a contingency for rig scarcity, not cost inflation; facility drawn on need. Management is raising debt from market and banks, with some funding from internal accruals post-workovers.

qa_highlights.question: Will gas realisation be disclosed by asset, and what are the asset-level prices?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO agreed to resume asset-wise realisation disclosure in the next presentation. B-80 gas about $16.5/MMBTU (exchange $15-16), Dirok about $12.5, PY-1 about $10-12; blended $12.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt is outstanding and when will cash flows fund capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Gearing 0.04; bank loan INR20 crore. Management says internal cash flows fund B-15 by around November-December 2027; B-80 programme relies on debt.

qa_highlights.question: Why not pass HPCL crude price loss to HPCL under the agreement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the agreement reversed the sale and HPCL is cooperative; a conciliation process under a High Court-appointed Chief Justice is pending, and HOEC will not renege on the agreed offtake.

risks_watch: B-80 HPCL crude: 85% still unsold, further mark-to-market loss of about 7-10% (not guidance), and a conciliation process with HPCL under a High Court-appointed Chief Justice.
Funding: B-80 workovers and three wells depend on debt being raised from the market; contingency capex increased versus Q4 due to rig scarcity.
Dirok: DNPL line degraded to ~1-1.5 MMSCMD versus 2.5 MMSCMD design; December 2026 hot-tap completion depends on AGCL and monsoon-hit timelines.
PY-1: two new wells deferred until a firm take-or-pay gas agreement with GAIL or IOCL; three wells previously suffered serious production loss.

Kharsang gas monetisation: 24 km pipeline needs forest clearances; 14-18 months timeline; virgin gas unsold meanwhile. Protest reported in Tamil Nadu over drilling in allocated area, to be managed with state government.
Track quarterly: B-80 water cut and workover results, actual B-80 production versus 8,900-13,000 bbl target, and asset-wise realisation disclosure promised for next presentation.
key_quotes: So our take is that by December, this should be completed.
But that said, we are producing only 50%-70% of the capability from the existing well stock because of the lack of evacuation route.
So for delivering B-80 program, we will have to rely on debt.
But please don't take it as a guidance.
We are on track to both grow value, create value as well as preserve value for our organization and for you shareholders.
summary.management_tone: Management is confident on long-term fundamentals and on the Dirok, B-80 and Kharsang plans, but cautious and at times evasive on HPCL crude losses, EBITDA ex-adjustments and the B-80 well-performance track record. Several timelines (December 2026 for hot taps, June 2027 for B-80 wells) are presented as targets with explicit caveats about delays.

growth.why: Q1 FY27 standalone revenue of INR117.5 crore rebounded from a negative Q4 only because of the HPCL crude reversal, while B-80 output fell on water cut and Dirok is producing only 50-70% of well capability; growth depends on B-80 workovers (Oct-Nov 2026), Dirok hot-tap (Dec 2026) and new wells by June 2027, all of which are debt- or rig-dependent and not yet quantified in revenue guidance.
